learningObjective: Use the four-question rehearsal cue, state, invariant, and move to rebuild a solution instead of memorizing its code.
mediumRationale: An original, phone-width explanatory drawing keeps the complete comparison visible without panning. A topic-specific timeline, quantity, evidence gate, or state relation replaces the component inventory. Geometry, direct labels, accessible descriptions, theme tokens, and static output carry the explanation without interaction.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: a process graph would show sequence but would not give each question a clear retrieval job.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected: the learning method is a set of readable prompts, not coordinate geometry.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected: semantic step panels keep the rehearsal usable at phone width, in print, and without color.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: the method should remain visible while the learner practices and should not hide its prompts behind controls.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the visual is an original synthesis of the supplied guide's learning method.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: prose names the four questions, but the visual sequence makes their order and handoff easier to retrieve.

deckReview.notes: No source slide deck is part of the supplied coding guide. The visual was designed from its cue, state, rule, move, and spaced-review method.

sourceReview.notes: The supplied Coding_Questions_Phone_Guide.md is the source for the method and practice sequence. No source artwork is reused.

agentReview.summary: Checked that the guide visual makes the retrieval loop explicit, names an invariant, and remains useful without depending on the exact wording of any one problem.

implementation.accessibility: For toy input four, two, seven and target nine, current index two contains seven. Nine minus seven is two. The earlier-value map contains four to index zero and two to index one. Looking up two returns one, so indices one and two identify two plus seven. The current index is absent during the query; insertion happens only after a miss. All labels use at least 12 viewBox units in a 360-unit-wide composition. Meaning is also encoded by positions, words, line styles, and numbers, not color alone.
